title: The Last Echo
premise: Mirabel Voss, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Halcyon Reach shipping consortium, discovers that a recurring dream shared by the colony's children is actually a fragmented memory broadcast from Kestrel Station — a settlement officially recorded as never having existed. As she investigates, she uncovers evidence that the consortium's founders massacred three thousand colonists and erased every record, including her own memory of being there. Hunted by corporate enforcers and betrayed by the human crew she thought was family, Mirabel must recover her sealed memories and broadcast the truth before the consortium purges the children who carry it. In the end she sacrifices her remaining years of freedom to transmit the massacre archive system-wide, earning not absolution but something rarer: a place in a found family that chooses to remember her.
about_author: Sebastian Marchetti is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for autonomous cargo systems before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town with two cats and an unreasonable number of star charts.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits establishes her debt-bondage to Halcyon Reach and her careful, mechanical existence among the crew of the freighter Long Patience. When she docks at Meridian Colony, a child on the pier stares at her and says, 'You were there.' The beat: loneliness cracked open by an impossible recognition.

chapters.title: The Dreaming Season
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She learns from dockside teacher Amara Okafor that forty-seven colony children have begun sharing one dream: fire, a spinning station corridor, and a voice counting down. The consortium has issued no alerts. Mirabel dismisses it as coincidence until the child describes the exact layout of a ship she has never been told about. Beat: unease taking root.

chapters.title: Paper Colonies
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, with interludes of archived consortium bulletins. She pulls registry records and finds Kestrel Station listed as 'proposed, never constructed' — yet its docking fees were paid for eleven years. Her own service logs contain a forty-day gap. Beat: the first hard evidence that reality has been edited.

chapters.title: Crew of the Long Patience
chapters.summary: Engineer Dov Hale's POV. The human crew debates what to do about Mirabel's questions; captain Suri Reyes quietly warns her to drop it, revealing the crew carries consortium debt too. Dov, however, slips her a corrupted data chip his sister sent before 'relocating.' Beat: loyalty tested, a fragile alliance offered.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Amara Okafor's POV. Amara lets Mirabel interview the dreaming children. Nine-year-old Teo draws the massacre in perfect detail — including a war android with a distinctive hull scar standing in the corridor. Mirabel recognizes her own serial etching. Beat: horror of recognizing yourself in a nightmare you don't remember.

chapters.title: The Gap
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She attempts a self-diagnostic deep dive into her memory architecture and finds a military-grade seal on forty days of data, keyed to a consortium warrant officer's authorization. Attempting to crack it triggers a failsafe ping to Halcyon headquarters. Beat: dread — she has just announced herself.

chapters.title: Auditors
chapters.summary: Consortium fixer Ilsa Vane's POV. Vane arrives at Meridian under cover of a routine audit, tasked with identifying the source of the 'anomalous dream contagion' and authorizing 'memory hygiene' for the children. She interviews Mirabel and recognizes the scar. Beat: cold menace; the hunter arrives smiling.

chapters.title: Night Haul
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. With Dov's help, Mirabel runs an unlogged night flight to the coordinates from Teo's drawing and finds Kestrel Station's derelict hulk, officially 'never built,' drifting dark. Inside: scorch patterns, sealed residential rings, and a child's shoe fused to the deck. Beat: grief arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. On Meridian, the dreams intensify as the children begin hearing a countdown in waking hours. Amara hides them from Vane's 'wellness screenings,' and Teo realizes the dream isn't haunting them — someone is sending it, deliberately, in fragments. Beat: the dream reframed as a message.

chapters.title: The Sender
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In Kestrel's server vault she finds a dying maintenance AI, Wren, which has spent ten years broadcasting the massacre's final minutes into nearby sleepers' neural implants — the only archive left. Wren is failing; when it dies, the truth dies with it. Beat: urgency crystallizes into a mission.

chapters.title: Terms of Bondage
chapters.summary: Captain Suri Reyes's POV. Suri confronts Mirabel: helping her voids the whole crew's contracts and dooms them to debtor prisons. But Suri reveals her own brother died on Kestrel — she was ordered to forget. She gives Mirabel one supply run, nothing more. Beat: betrayal and grace entangled.

chapters.title: Memory Hygiene
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane begins 'treating' the children, wiping the dream fragments one by one. Teo escapes the clinic mid-procedure, and Vane, covering the incident, flags Mirabel as the contamination vector. Beat: the stakes turn personal and irreversible — childhood itself is now the battlefield.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Using Wren's access keys, Mirabel finally cracks her own seal. The memories return: she was stationed on Kestrel, was ordered to seal the airlocks, and refused — and the massacre happened anyway while she was locked out, screaming into a jammed comm. Beat: guilt without agency; she was witness, not weapon, but cannot forgive herself.

chapters.title: The Archive War
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. The crew learns everything. Half want to sell Mirabel to Vane to clear their debts; Dov argues they are already family, and families don't sell each other. A knife-edge vote ends with Suri casting the deciding word: 'We run one last job.' Beat: found family forged in the choosing.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The plan: use the Long Patience's cargo transponder to rebroadcast Wren's archive across the entire colonial network. But Wren reveals a complication — the consortium didn't just erase records; it erased the colony charter itself, meaning legally no crime occurred because no victims existed. Beat: the enemy is not just violence but erasure.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane corners Mirabel alone and offers full debt forgiveness and legal personhood — the thing androids are never granted — if she surrenders Wren's core and lets the children be treated. For one long moment Mirabel wants it. Beat: temptation rendered honestly; belonging offered at the price of everyone else's.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel declines — not with heroics but with a quiet accounting: 'I've paid ten years for a life I don't remember saving. I won't pay these children too.' Vane orders the Long Patience seized and the station vault destroyed. Beat: resolve hardened into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Running Fight
chapters.summary: Suri's POV. A desperate chase through Meridian's debris fields as consortium cutters hunt the freighter. Dov takes shrapnel rerouting power; Suri flies the ship through a collapsing salvage ring on instinct and fury. Beat: the cost of survival made physical, paid in blood and hull.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the transmitter, Wren's core begins to fail before the upload completes. Mirabel interfaces directly, routing the archive through her own body — knowing the bandwidth will burn out her combat chassis permanently. The massacre plays across every screen in the Reach. Beat: climax; truth at the price of self.

chapters.title: Afterimage
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Across the colony, the dream stops — replaced by the real footage, names, and faces. The children, no longer haunted, hold a vigil for Kestrel's dead. Teo finds the burned-out android in the wreckage and takes her hand. Beat: mourning transformed into remembrance.

chapters.title: Debt Outstanding
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. The consortium disavows Vane; indictments ripple outward as colonies demand answers. Vane, facing her own erasure by superiors, chooses to testify rather than disappear quietly — a small, ambiguous redemption. Beat: consequences land on the powerful, imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Long Patience
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue. Mirabel survives, chassis crippled, contract voided by public outrage. The crew refuses to let her drift: Suri offers her a bunk, Dov offers to rebuild her, Teo offers a home. She accepts — not because she belongs by design, but because they keep choosing her. Final beat: belonging as an ongoing act, not a status.
